info.title: OwnBase REST API
info.description:
The REST routes under /api/ that the first-party clients use, and the Slack-compatible methods apps call. The native routes are not a stable public API: they change with the clients, and the version here is the client protocol's (`PROTOCOL_VERSION`). docs/INTEGRATIONS.md is the contract for apps.

Generated from the endpoint table in @ownbase/protocol and the zod schemas the server validates requests with, by packages/server/test/openapi.test.ts, which fails when this file is out of date. Rewrite it with `pnpm --filter @ownbase/server exec vitest run test/openapi.test.ts -u`.

The WebSocket at /ws, incoming webhooks at /hooks/, the web client's files and the enterprise edition's routes are not described here.

get.summary: Whether the server is up and its database answers.
get.description:
Whether the server is up and its database answers. `instanceId` is new each time the server starts, so a host can tell its own server from another one on the same port.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

get.summary: The STUN and TURN servers calls connect through.
get.description:
The STUN and TURN servers calls connect through. A TURN relay the server shares a secret with gets a password made for the caller, which runs out.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

get.summary: What this server is, before anyone signs in: its name, versions, who may join, whether it still needs a claim code, and any other way to sign in.
get.description:
What this server is, before anyone signs in: its name, versions, who may join, whether it still needs a claim code, and any other way to sign in.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

get.summary: The workspace's icon, for anyone: the Join screen shows it beside the workspace's name before anyone signs in.
get.description:
The workspace's icon, for anyone: the Join screen shows it beside the workspace's name before anyone signs in. Its type is the one its bytes were checked to be. Asked for by its current version, the answer never changes, since another picture has another version, so it is kept for a year; asked for otherwise, it is checked again each time.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

post.summary: Creates an account with a password and signs it in.
post.description:
Creates an account with a password and signs it in. The first account owns the workspace, and needs the claim code unless it is made on the host's own machine. After that, an invite-only workspace needs an invite code.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

post.summary: Joining with a display name alone, where the host allows guests.
post.description:
Joining with a display name alone, where the host allows guests. The policy is read inside the same write that creates the guest, so a page that still says guests are welcome cannot let one in after the host said no. Rationed by address like any sign-in, and bounded in number.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

post.summary: A guest keeping who they are as an account: same id, so their messages and rooms stay theirs.
post.description:
A guest keeping who they are as an account: same id, so their messages and rooms stay theirs. Only while accounts can be created without an invite, and a new session replaces every guest one.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

post.summary: Signs in with a handle and password.
post.description:
Signs in with a handle and password. An account with two-step sign-in gets a challenge instead of a session, which `two-step` answers.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

post.summary: The second step of signing in (E11): a code from the authenticator app, each step's once, or a recovery code, each once.
post.description:
The second step of signing in (E11): a code from the authenticator app, each step's once, or a recovery code, each once. A few wrong ones send the person back to their password.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

post.summary: Signs out the session the request carries, and closes its live connection.
post.description:
Signs out the session the request carries, and closes its live connection.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

post.summary: Changing a password proves you know the current one, then signs out everywhere else.
post.description:
Changing a password proves you know the current one, then signs out everywhere else. A password is usually changed because someone else might know it; leaving their sessions running would defeat the whole exercise.

Needs a signed-in account.

get.description:

Needs a signed-in account.

post.description:

get.summary: A window of history centred on one message, for a search hit, a pin or a link.
get.description:
A window of history centred on one message, for a search hit, a pin or a link. For a reply, the window is centred on its thread's first message.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

get.summary: A window of history centred on the first message after `seq`, where someone who had read up to it takes up reading again.
get.description:
A window of history centred on the first message after `seq`, where someone who had read up to it takes up reading again. A conversation with more unread than one page opens there, at its New line, not at the newest. Their own messages are skipped: 404 when nobody else has written since.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

get.summary: One message, for the card under a link to it.
get.description:
One message, for the card under a link to it. Asked by each reader, so a message in a private conversation shows only to the people in it.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

get.summary: The messages after one, newest first, for scrolling back down towards the latest.
get.description:
The messages after one, newest first, for scrolling back down towards the latest.

patch.summary: Changes the words of the caller's own message.
patch.description:
Changes the words of the caller's own message. `expectedText` is what they started from, so an edit made meanwhile elsewhere is not overwritten. Polls and call notes cannot be changed.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

delete.summary: Deletes a message and its files, the caller's own or, for an admin, anyone's.
delete.description:
Deletes a message and its files, the caller's own or, for an admin, anyone's. Deleting a thread's first message deletes its replies too.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

post.summary: Reports a message to the workspace's admins (E12), by anyone who can read it but its author.
post.description:
Reports a message to the workspace's admins (E12), by anyone who can read it but its author. Reporting it again while the first report is open changes nothing, and its author is told nothing.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

get.summary: A preview's picture, for whoever can read its message.
get.description:
A preview's picture, for whoever can read its message. The server fetched it and checked its first bytes; it is sent as the type those bytes say, never sniffed again by the browser, and kept by nothing on the way.

Needs a signed-in account.

delete.description:

get.description:
A file's bytes, for whoever can read its conversation. With the session header it opens in place; with `?download=<ticket>` it saves under its name.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

put.summary: Adds the caller's reaction to a message.
put.description:
Adds the caller's reaction to a message. Adding one they already made changes nothing.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

delete.summary: Takes the caller's reaction off a message.
delete.description:
Takes the caller's reaction off a message.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

put.description:
A voter's choices, replacing any before; none takes the vote back. Readers are told the new count by a `message.updated` that says `pollOnly`, and the voter's own devices what they chose, which an anonymous poll says to nobody.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

post.summary: Its author closes a poll for good: the votes stand and nobody can change them.
post.description:
Its author closes a poll for good: the votes stand and nobody can change them.

get.summary: For the owner and admins: whether the server is keeping up, from counts, sizes and times alone.
get.description:
For the owner and admins: whether the server is keeping up, from counts, sizes and times alone. Nothing from a conversation, an app's delivery error or a credential is in it.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

get.summary: The owner's downloadable copy of the workspace: being made, ready, failed, or none.
get.description:
The owner's downloadable copy of the workspace: being made, ready, failed, or none.

post.summary: Starts making a copy of the whole workspace for the owner to download, after checking the server has the disk space for it.
post.description:
Starts making a copy of the whole workspace for the owner to download, after checking the server has the disk space for it. A copy already being made is returned instead of a second one.

post.summary: A one-time ticket for downloading the ready copy by a plain link.
post.description:
A one-time ticket for downloading the ready copy by a plain link.

get.summary: The copy as one zip.
get.description:
The copy as one zip. A ticket stands in for the header a download in the browser cannot carry, and whoever spends it must still be the owner, signed in with the session that asked for it.

Needs the workspace owner.

get.summary: For the owner and admins: what happened in huddles lately (see `CallLog`), in the conversations they can see themselves.
get.description:
For the owner and admins: what happened in huddles lately (see `CallLog`), in the conversations they can see themselves. Memory only.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: Makes an app with its own bot user.
post.description:
Makes an app with its own bot user. The answer holds its `xoxb-` bot token, which is shown this once, and the signing secret.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

get.summary: Every app, newest first, with its webhooks, commands, event subscriptions and signing secret.
get.description:
Every app, newest first, with its webhooks, commands, event subscriptions and signing secret.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

put.summary: What an app may do (E18c): Slack's scope names, replacing the whole list.
put.description:
What an app may do (E18c): Slack's scope names, replacing the whole list. Its tokens hold the new list from the next call; events already queued for it were let through under the old one and are still sent.

Logged with what was added and taken away, which is what an operator looks for when an app starts or stops seeing something.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: A new bot token, replacing every one the app had.
post.description:
A new bot token, replacing every one the app had. For a token that has leaked, and for an admin who closed the dialog before copying the one they were shown at creation, which is otherwise a working app nobody can use.

Logged without the token: who replaced which app's credentials is what an operator wants to find afterwards.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: A new signing secret.
post.description:
A new signing secret. Every request signed from here on uses it, including event deliveries already waiting in the queue, which are signed when they are sent rather than when they were queued. The app refuses them until it has the new secret, which is the point when the old one has leaked.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

delete.summary: Deletes an app with its tokens, webhooks, commands and event subscriptions.
delete.description:
Deletes an app with its tokens, webhooks, commands and event subscriptions. What its bot posted stays.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: Makes an incoming webhook that posts to one channel as the app's bot, and adds the bot to that channel.
post.description:
Makes an incoming webhook that posts to one channel as the app's bot, and adds the bot to that channel. The URL is shown this once.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: A new URL for an existing webhook.
post.description:
A new URL for an existing webhook. The secret is the whole of a webhook's authority, so a URL pasted somewhere public has to be replaceable without removing the webhook and choosing its channel again.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

delete.summary: Deletes an incoming webhook.
delete.description:
Deletes an incoming webhook. Its URL stops working at once.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: Slack's auth.test.
post.description:
Slack's auth.test. Bolt calls it before it will start, and gives up if it fails, so without it no Bolt app could run against this server at all. `bot_id` is the app's id: this server has no separate bot identity.

Called with an app's bot token, as Slack's Web API is. A failure is HTTP 200 with `ok: false`.

requestBody.description: Slack's arguments for this method, as listed in docs/INTEGRATIONS.md.

post.description:
Slack Web API compatible send, so existing bot code works by pointing at this server. Errors use Slack's `{ok:false, error}` shape.

Called with an app's bot token, as Slack's Web API is. A failure is HTTP 200 with `ok: false`.

post.description:
Gives an app a slash command, posted to its URL when someone types it. A name already taken, or built in, is refused.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

Removes an app's slash command.

get.description:
Every command anyone can run, for the composer's hint list.

Needs a signed-in account. Guests may call it too.

post.description:
Runs `/whatever …` typed in a channel.

post.description:
Slack's `response_url`: how an app replies after its first few seconds.

Anyone may call this, signed in or not.

get.summary: What administrators have changed, newest first, for a workspace that has to be able to say who deactivated someone or replaced an app's token.
get.description:
What administrators have changed, newest first, for a workspace that has to be able to say who deactivated someone or replaced an app's token.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

get.summary: Everyone with an account, for an admin who has to run this workspace: what they can do, when they were last seen, and whether they use two-step sign-in.
get.description:
Everyone with an account, for an admin who has to run this workspace: what they can do, when they were last seen, and whether they use two-step sign-in. Bots are in the list because a forgotten bot is exactly the account worth noticing.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

patch.summary: Change what someone can do, or take their access away.
patch.description:
Change what someone can do, or take their access away.

The rules are about who may act on whom, and they are deliberately narrow: the owner is untouchable and cannot be locked out of their own server, an admin cannot demote or deactivate another admin (a workspace should not be losable to an argument between two of them), and nobody can act on themselves — an admin cannot quietly promote themselves to owner or lock themselves out by accident.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: Password recovery for an installation with no email: an admin issues a temporary password and reads it to the person over whatever channel they trust.
post.description:
Password recovery for an installation with no email: an admin issues a temporary password and reads it to the person over whatever channel they trust. It is shown once, all their sessions end, and they are expected to change it. Who may be reset is resettable's to say.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: Turns someone's two-step sign-in off, for one who lost their authenticator app and recovery codes (E11).
post.description:
Turns someone's two-step sign-in off, for one who lost their authenticator app and recovery codes (E11). Their devices stay signed in; their next sign-in asks for the password alone, and they can set it up again.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

get.summary: The reported messages waiting for an admin (E12), each with its reports: the message itself even from a conversation the admin is not in, since whoever repor…
get.description:
The reported messages waiting for an admin (E12), each with its reports: the message itself even from a conversation the admin is not in, since whoever reported it showed it to them, and null once its author deleted it.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: Settles a reported message (E12): dismissed, removed, or removed with its author deactivated, by People's rules for deactivating.
post.description:
Settles a reported message (E12): dismissed, removed, or removed with its author deactivated, by People's rules for deactivating. Every open report of it closes, and the record says what was done and to whom, never what the message said.

Needs an administrator or the owner.

post.summary: Hands the workspace to someone else.
post.description:
Hands the workspace to someone else. Only the owner can do it, and they become an admin rather than losing their access — a workspace with no owner is the state this whole area exists to prevent.

Needs the workspace owner.

put.summary: The workspace's name, for its owner and admins.

post.summary: Slack's views.update: changes a form the person still has open, without a trigger, which is how an app shows "Loading" at once and the real form when it has it.
post.description:
Slack's views.update: changes a form the person still has open, without a trigger, which is how an app shows "Loading" at once and the real form when it has it. What they typed into an input that keeps its block and action ids stays, as on Slack. A `hash` from an earlier answer refuses the change if the view has changed since, so two updates cannot cross.

Called with an app's bot token, as Slack's Web API is. A failure is HTTP 200 with `ok: false`.
